en: O Canada! land of our forefathers,
Your brow is wreathed with glorious flowers.
For your arm knows how to carry the sword,
It knows how to carry the cross;
Your history is an epic
Of the most brilliant deeds;
And your valour, steeped in faith,
Will protect our homes and our rights.
Under the eye of God, beside the giant river,
The Canadian grows in hope.
He is born of a proud race;
Blessed was his cradle.
Heaven has marked out his course
In this new world:
Always guided by its light,
He will keep the honour of his flag.
From his patron, forerunner of the true God,
He bears on his brow the halo of fire.
Enemy of tyranny,
But full of loyalty,
He knows how to keep in harmony
His proud liberty,
And by the effort of his genius
To set truth firmly on our soil.
Sacred love of the throne and of the altar,
Fill our hearts with your immortal breath.
Among the foreign races
Our guide is the law;
Let us know how to be a people of brothers
Under the yoke of the Faith;
And let us repeat like our fathers
The conquering cry: For Christ and the King!
notes: line 1.2: 'fleurons', the flower-shaped ornaments of a crown or wreath.
line 2.1: the giant river is the St. Lawrence.
line 2.7: 'sa lumière', its light: the light of heaven (or His, God's).
line 3.1: the patron is St John the Baptist, patron saint of French Canadians, the forerunner of Christ.
line 3.8: 'asseoir', to seat or establish firmly.
